Kempton Park's Haunted Hospital

By: Catherine Rice | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Dubbed South Africa's ghost hospital, the Kempton Park hospital closed in 1996. Since then it's become a destination for thrill seekers, but its draining millions from the public purse.

Unique Selling Point:
Kempton Park Hospital, a vast, decaying landmark closed suddenly in 1996 and was left to rot for nearly three decades. Once a state-of-the-art facility, it is now dubbed South Africa’s “ghost hospital,” known as much for its haunted reputation and thrill-seeking trespassers as for the millions it still drains from the public purse.



Summary:
The hospital has become the stuff of legend. Ghostly sightings and a disgraced doctor have become folklore and paranormal “hunters” allegedly bribe guards to gain access. On the social media platform TikTok, dozens of videos showing the inside of the hospital have been posted. Comments on the posts indicate security guards were bribed between R50 and R150 to gain access.

The Gauteng Department of Health spends over five million rand a year on security (revealed in a provincial legislature reply), yet the site has been stripped bare. Patients at Tembisa Hospital just 22 minutes away sleep on chairs and floors. Those living in Kempton Park are referred to Tembisa hospital, where conditions are dire.

Yet, the Heatlh Department’s promises to refurbish the Kempton Park hospital have come to nothing. Ideas of refurbishing, demolishing or rebuilding, have gone nowhere. Costs ranged from 1,7 billion to 3,6 billion. Costs for security have ballooned to R35 million since its closure in 1996.
The Democratic Alliance's Michael Waters, who inspected the site recently, said the building is an empty shell, with broken windows, ripped-out electrical outlets, smashed furniture and graffiti on the walls. He said it's clear the building has been illegally invaded, and something needs to be done urgently.

Mother nature has taken over the site, and its clear that money is not being spent on the grounds. This is visible outside the hospital, where the land has become completely overgrown.

Ghost tour operators have been doing tours of the hospital - a content creation company called Space did a series of videos of haunted places in Joburg, and visited Kempton Park hospital with a ghost tour operator. The videos show clear evidence of ash from recently burnt fires. It's seems access, if you are willing to bribe the security guards, is not an issue. On Halloween, it apparently gets very busy as hunters of the paranormal seek their thrills at the abandoned hospital.


Further information:
We speak to the DA's Michael Waters about the millions being drained from the public purse, we also speak to ghost tour operator Nigel Mullinder and surgeon Dr Nick Wolmarans who worked at the hospital for a decade. Local GPs complain that they must refer Kempton Park patients to Tembisa hospital, when once they could simply send them to the Kempton Park hospital, a state of the art facility. We also gain access to the hospital ourselves and interview officials at the Gauteng department of Health about their plans for its future. Despite being given the run around, we are finally given access to the premises on the 13th of November with a delegation from the health department to escort us. The department denies bribery is happening, and say since they took over the security at the hospital in September 2024, with a company called Special Arrow Trade and Projects, the vandalism has stopped.

In a response to a question in the provincial legislature, the Gauteng Health Department said it is still weighing options for the long-abandoned Kempton Park Hospital, with costs estimated at R1.76 billion to refurbish or R3.6 billion to demolish and rebuild. An Expression of Interest has been advertised to test private sector partnerships and alternative funding. Meanwhile, the facility continues to drain public funds, with R5.3 million spent on security in 2024/25 alone, bringing the total since May 2024 to R5.8 million. Nearby hospitals strain under pressure — Tembisa has 840 beds and Edenvale just 230 - underscoring the urgent need for decisive action on the so-called “ghost hospital.”

Script:


NATSOUND: Male voice (Subtitles): With multiple six-floor buildings to scale and zero safety precautions, one wrong foot could literally lead to death.

Male voice (Subtitles): I’ve got range. Let’s go for these stairs. Oh, s**t! Maybe not.

VO 1 Players armed with replica rifles navigate corridors and crumbling wards in a game known as Airsoft.

VO 2 Since this hospital closed its doors almost three decades ago, its become a magnet for thrill seekers.

NATSOUND Subtitles: Hello! Are you human?

VO 3 …and ghost hunters.

NATSOUND Subtitles: We’re a big group.

VO 4 Criminals have stripped it completely. Its wards now hosting everything from drug use to whispered tales of satanic rituals.

VO 5 Welcome to the abandoned Kempton Park hospital.

FADE TO BLACK

UPSOUND Dr Nick Womarans / Surgeon: This was the only hospital in Kempton Park. It was a government hospital. It had good staff, excellent doctors. It was a general hospital, it had orthopaedics, it had surgery, excellent paediatric unit.

VO 6 Dr Nick Wolmarans is a surgeon who worked at Kempton Park Hospital from the mid eighties until it closed in 1996. Located on Joburg’s East Rand, it was a centre of medical excellence.

UPSOUND Dr Nick Wolmarans / Surgeon: It was very busy. I sometimes had to go and do my cases in a different hospital just because I couldn’t get a bed.

VO 7 His memories of that time are now overshadowed by what it’s become.

UPSOUND Nick Wolmarans / Surgeon: I’m extremely sad, because you know, it was 100 meters from my practice. The staff were really old school, the control of the quality was taken care of. If a sister called you, and says she’s got a problem, then you better go ‘cos they were well trained.

GOVAN: What do you think of the state that it’s in now?

UPSOUND Nick Wolmarans / Surgeon: It’s very bad. I’ve been in there and I cannot see that that place can be repaired.

LINK Kempton Park hospital was built in the 1970s and opened in 1978. It had 350 beds.

VO 8 Since it’s closure, the closest major hospital for Kempton Park residents is Tembisa hospital, which has 840 beds.

VO 9 It’s overburdened, buckling under the strain. It’s also at the centre of a two billion rand looting scandal.

NATSOUND: This is not on.

VO 10 This video of conditions at Tembisa was widely shared just a few weeks ago.

NATSOUND: Subtitles: Guys, I'm here at Tembisa Hospital right now as we speak.
Look how our human beings are being, I may call it, stored.

VO 11 So why hasn’t there been more urgency to restore Kempton Park hospital to its former glory?

VO 12 For years, there’ve been calls for the hospital to reopen. The DA’s Michael Waters has been asking questions in the provincial legislature.

UPSOUND Michael Waters / DA MPL: The MEC replied that if they were to refurbish the hospital it would cost R1,8 billion roughly and if they were to knock it down and rebuild a brand new hospital it would cost R3.6 billion.

VO 13 The Gauteng health department also revealed staggering security costs.

UPSOUND Michael Waters: There is a security company, believe it or not, and that’s costing the taxpayer R5,6 million a year.

VO 14 Waters says the decision to close the hospital was shortsighted.

UPSOUND Michael Waters / DA Member: Gauteng Provincial Legislature: They probably thought they had enough beds in Tembisa for the population at the time, not taking into consideration population growth. And we all know what’s happening at the Tembisa hospital. It’s infamous now, not only for corruption, for fires, for people being murdered.

VO 15 Among those controversies was the murder of Babita Deokaran, a whistleblower within the Gauteng Health Department who was assassinated in 2021 after uncovering alleged tender corruption at Tembisa Hospital

UPSOUND: Michael Waters: The fact is that patients are laying on the floors because there are no beds available.

GOVAN: So they need this hospital?

UPSOUND Michael Waters: Desperately. They don’t even need it. It’s a matter of life and death literally.

NATSOUND This was the old emergency room.

VO 16 Earlier this year, Waters went inside the hospital for an oversight visit. We also wanted to see inside - and so arrange access.

VO 17 But when we arrive, security guards refuse to allow us in, despite the Gauteng Health department granting permission to our producer the previous week.

VO 18 It seems the Health MEC’s assistant, Tinyiko Manyisa, has had a change of heart.

NATSOUND Subtitle: Hello
Govan: Hi Mr Manyisa, I‘m calling to find out what went wrong. You initially said we could come to the hospital and see inside and now it seems like we’re not allowed or what’s the story?
Mr Manyisa: Subtitles: No, no, no. We might have had a communication breakdown.
Govan: Could you tell me why we can’t go inside, sir?
Mr Manyisa: It’s not safe.
Govan: But you’ve had a number of oversight inspections inside the hospital so it was safe enough for them.
Mr Manyisa: Subtitles: The team that is responsible for safety has to be on site.

VO 19 While these may be valid reasons, it’s ironic that members of the public can seemingly gain access with an exchange of cash, while members of the media are blocked.

NATSOUND Security guard: Subtitles: My friend, what I can tell you, neh... It's for your own safety.
Govan: But people do go in for ghost tours.
Security guard: Subtitles: Why are you not going inside if you are doing that?
Govan: Because I'm not paying a bribe.
Security guard: Subtiltes: No, we don't do such.

LINK: But they do do ghost tours here. I know that cos I’ve seen it on Tiktok. Touchy subject, bribing.

NATSOUND: Subtitles: What was that? A fluorescent tube breaking? You tell me.

VO 20 Nigel Mullinder says he was there just two months ago. By day he has an ordinary job, but at night he’s a paranormal investigator, and does ghost tours. He doesn’t charge his clients, but they have to pay security for access.

UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder / Paranormal Investigator: It’s seen now as sort of like an entrance fee. It’s the only way security will come to the gate is if you say I’m going to give you a hundred bucks per person or whatever they feel like on the night.

NATSOUND: Subtitles: Hmmm, it says 'Dead Inside".

VO 21 Nigel has been visiting the hospital for the past sixteen years, since he was a teenager.

UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: I mean I know the place like the back of my hand. You ask me any place in that hospital I can tell you where it is.

GOVAN: How many times have you been in the hospital?

UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: So its about 130 plus times that I’ve been to Kempton Park Hospital. Holds a very special place in my heart as one of the first sort of abandoned places where I had a tangible experience as a paranormal investigator. My first adrenaline rush. It really holds something towards me, ja.

VO 22 It’s changed a lot since he first visited.

UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: The first time I went into the Kempton Park hospital there was a lot of old medical equipment. Eerie. You know, I mean you had back boards, and neck braces and baby incubators just lying around.

GOVAN: And now?

UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: It’s been stripped. They’ve allowed people to come into there and chip the steel piping out of the walls. I mean that shows a different level of we didn’t look, we didn’t see.

VO 23 Despite the run around, we’re finally given access a week later. Invited back to see for ourselves, with a Gauteng health department delegation to escort us, for our own safety.

Govan: I didn’t know you needed PPE in this hospital. I don’t think I’ve ever seen anyone wearing PPE who’s been in here.

VO 24 Gauteng Health MEC Nomantu Nkomo-Ralehoko is also in attendance.

VO 25 The Gauteng Health department’s deputy-director general of infrastructure, Xolisani Galada, says the hospital was closed down for good reason in 1996.

UPSOUND Xolisani Galada: I think the leadership at the time realised it was being under utilised and I think it was beginning to be costly to maintain the services when there were a lack of patients coming in. So, a decision was then taken.

VO 26 But, he recognises that there is now a shortage of hospitals in the province.

UPSOUND Xolisani Galada: We have got plans that we want to revamp the hospital. We are looking at various options as we speak. We have approached private sector in coming and partnering with us in making sure that this particular asset is revamped and brought back. Already we have received about four proposals.

VO 27 The Gauteng health department took over security at the hospital in September last year. Before that, it was the responsibility of the department of infrastructure, absolving the health department, according to them, of any prior responsibility.

UPSOUND Xolisani Galada: All government assets, the custodian is the Gauteng department of infrastructure. All of them. However, in this instance we have taken over because we see we want to preserve this asset. We want to intervene and refurbish this asset, and that’s why we have taken over including the issues around security and all of that. The property previously was vandalised. We came in, we made sure that we stopped the vandalism.

VO 28 It may be too late for preservation, but Galada insists officers at the security company, Special Arrow Trade and Projects, don't take bribes.

Govan: You know they do ghost tours here. R100 each to the security at the gate.
Xolisani Galada: I think we can categorically deny that.
Govan: You don’t think that happens?
Xolisani Galada: Since we have taken over the security, we have never had a report that says there are people doing ghost tours here. We are not aware of that.

VO 29 The interview takes a hostile turn and tensions escalate quickly, as I try to show them recent videos of ghost tours on the premises.

UPSOUND Nomantu Nkomo-Ralehoko / Gauteng Health MEC: It’s not going to be a one sided interview. I want to make it clear to yourselves now. You are going to complete it properly, Govan. If you don’t I’m going to fight you guys. I’m tired of people making allegations about the department of health.

VO 30 They also insist the security contract is above board.

UPSOUND Xolisani Galanda: This has got nothing to do as a comparison with Tembisa. It’s a complete different thing what happened in Tembisa. Here you have a legitimate contract.

VO 31 I’m told the videos had been filmed before September 2024, and simply reposted.

Govan: It’s posted on the 27th of the tenth. No, it’s been posted on the 27th of the 10th, 2024.
Woman: You are confused. You are confused.
Govan: Show me.
Woman: You don’t know Twitter.
Govan: The last ghost tour that happened here was two months ago.
Woman: Allegation. It’s alleged. Shall I go to the dictionary and define what allegation means?

VO 32 And then something that has never happened to me before.

UPSOUND Man: Subtitles: Our officers are informing us you were here two weeks back. You tried to bribe your way in.
Govan: Who?
Male: You
Govan: None of our interactions with them weren’t on camera. I want you to know that everything I said to you was on camera neh, and now you’re saying to him that I tried to bribe you. Rember that please.
Woman: But Govan, you see now you are saying it’s alleged. We’ll ask them to do an affidavit of what they are telling us, so that we will also be able to email it to your bosses.
Govan: And in response to the affidavit I will be able to submit the footage. The footage which is undisputed.
Woman: Yes.

LINK: Luckily we have the recordings. And they speak for themselves.

NATSOUND: Govan: Can we get someone just to take us around just to go inside. We want to go and look for that ghost.

VO 33 Mother Nature has reclaimed this land. The hospital now a monument to decay and neglect. It’s hard to imagine its doors ever reopening.

LINK: What I can see here is that this place is not unoccupied. People are coming through here. This is cables that have been stripped. You see. That has nothing to do with ghosts. That’s criminality.

VO 34 For Dr Nick Wolmarans, Kempton Park Hospital isn’t just an abandoned building. It’s a painful symbol of squandered resources and a system failing the people it was meant to serve.

UPSOUND Dr Nick Wolmarans: It’s a shame that a hospital and a facility went down the drain. I'm very concerned. I’ve been to a few of the government hospitals and I must tell you. (Subtitles) You must take your Bible and pray.

GOVAN: So they need this hospital? UPSOUND Michael Waters: Desperately. They don’t even need it. It’s a matter of life and death literally. NATSOUND This was the old emergency room. VO 16 Earlier this year, Waters went inside the hospital for an oversight visit. We also wanted to see inside - and so arrange access. VO 17 But when we arrive, security guards refuse to allow us in, despite the Gauteng Health department granting permission to our producer the previous week. VO 18 It seems the Health MEC’s assistant, Tinyiko Manyisa, has had a change of heart. NATSOUND Subtitle: Hello Govan: Hi Mr Manyisa, I‘m calling to find out what went wrong. You initially said we could come to the hospital and see inside and now it seems like we’re not allowed or what’s the story? Mr Manyisa: Subtitles: No, no, no. We might have had a communication breakdown. Govan: Could you tell me why we can’t go inside, sir? Mr Manyisa: It’s not safe. Govan: But you’ve had a number of oversight inspections inside the hospital so it was safe enough for them. Mr Manyisa: Subtitles: The team that is responsible for safety has to be on site. VO 19 While these may be valid reasons, it’s ironic that members of the public can seemingly gain access with an exchange of cash, while members of the media are blocked. NATSOUND Security guard: Subtitles: My friend, what I can tell you, neh... It's for your own safety. Govan: But people do go in for ghost tours. Security guard: Subtitles: Why are you not going inside if you are doing that? Govan: Because I'm not paying a bribe. Security guard: Subtiltes: No, we don't do such. LINK: But they do do ghost tours here. I know that cos I’ve seen it on Tiktok. Touchy subject, bribing. NATSOUND: Subtitles: What was that? A fluorescent tube breaking? You tell me. VO 20 Nigel Mullinder says he was there just two months ago. By day he has an ordinary job, but at night he’s a paranormal investigator, and does ghost tours. He doesn’t charge his clients, but they have to pay security for access. UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder / Paranormal Investigator: It’s seen now as sort of like an entrance fee. It’s the only way security will come to the gate is if you say I’m going to give you a hundred bucks per person or whatever they feel like on the night. NATSOUND: Subtitles: Hmmm, it says 'Dead Inside". VO 21 Nigel has been visiting the hospital for the past sixteen years, since he was a teenager. UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: I mean I know the place like the back of my hand. You ask me any place in that hospital I can tell you where it is. GOVAN: How many times have you been in the hospital? UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: So its about 130 plus times that I’ve been to Kempton Park Hospital. Holds a very special place in my heart as one of the first sort of abandoned places where I had a tangible experience as a paranormal investigator. My first adrenaline rush. It really holds something towards me, ja. VO 22 It’s changed a lot since he first visited. UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: The first time I went into the Kempton Park hospital there was a lot of old medical equipment. Eerie. You know, I mean you had back boards, and neck braces and baby incubators just lying around. GOVAN: And now? UPSOUND Nigel Mullinder: It’s been stripped. They’ve allowed people to come into there and chip the steel piping out of the walls. I mean that shows a different level of we didn’t look, we didn’t see. VO 23 Despite the run around, we’re finally given access a week later. Invited back to see for ourselves, with a Gauteng health department delegation to escort us, for our own safety. Govan: I didn’t know you needed PPE in this hospital. I don’t think I’ve ever seen anyone wearing PPE who’s been in here. VO 24 Gauteng Health MEC Nomantu Nkomo-Ralehoko is also in attendance. VO 25 The Gauteng Health department’s deputy-director general of infrastructure, Xolisani Galada, says the hospital was closed down for good reason in 1996. UPSOUND Xolisani Galada: I think the leadership at the time realised it was being under utilised and I think it was beginning to be costly to maintain the services when there were a lack of patients coming in. So, a decision was then taken. VO 26 But, he recognises that there is now a shortage of hospitals in the province. UPSOUND Xolisani Galada: We have got plans that we want to revamp the hospital. We are looking at various options as we speak. We have approached private sector in coming and partnering with us in making sure that this particular asset is revamped and brought back. Already we have received about four proposals. VO 27 The Gauteng health department took over security at the hospital in September last year. Before that, it was the responsibility of the department of infrastructure, absolving the health department, according to them, of any prior responsibility. UPSOUND Xolisani Galada: All government assets, the custodian is the Gauteng department of infrastructure. All of them. However, in this instance we have taken over because we see we want to preserve this asset. We want to intervene and refurbish this asset, and that’s why we have taken over including the issues around security and all of that. The property previously was vandalised. We came in, we made sure that we stopped the vandalism. VO 28 It may be too late for preservation, but Galada insists officers at the security company, Special Arrow Trade and Projects, don't take bribes. Govan: You know they do ghost tours here. R100 each to the security at the gate. Xolisani Galada: I think we can categorically deny that. Govan: You don’t think that happens? Xolisani Galada: Since we have taken over the security, we have never had a report that says there are people doing ghost tours here. We are not aware of that. VO 29 The interview takes a hostile turn and tensions escalate quickly, as I try to show them recent videos of ghost tours on the premises. UPSOUND Nomantu Nkomo-Ralehoko / Gauteng Health MEC: It’s not going to be a one sided interview. I want to make it clear to yourselves now. You are going to complete it properly, Govan. If you don’t I’m going to fight you guys. I’m tired of people making allegations about the department of health. VO 30 They also insist the security contract is above board. UPSOUND Xolisani Galanda: This has got nothing to do as a comparison with Tembisa. It’s a complete different thing what happened in Tembisa. Here you have a legitimate contract. VO 31 I’m told the videos had been filmed before September 2024, and simply reposted. Govan: It’s posted on the 27th of the tenth. No, it’s been posted on the 27th of the 10th, 2024. Woman: You are confused. You are confused. Govan: Show me. Woman: You don’t know Twitter. Govan: The last ghost tour that happened here was two months ago. Woman: Allegation. It’s alleged. Shall I go to the dictionary and define what allegation means? VO 32 And then something that has never happened to me before. UPSOUND Man: Subtitles: Our officers are informing us you were here two weeks back. You tried to bribe your way in. Govan: Who? Male: You Govan: None of our interactions with them weren’t on camera. I want you to know that everything I said to you was on camera neh, and now you’re saying to him that I tried to bribe you. Rember that please. Woman: But Govan, you see now you are saying it’s alleged. We’ll ask them to do an affidavit of what they are telling us, so that we will also be able to email it to your bosses. Govan: And in response to the affidavit I will be able to submit the footage. The footage which is undisputed. Woman: Yes. LINK: Luckily we have the recordings. And they speak for themselves. NATSOUND: Govan: Can we get someone just to take us around just to go inside. We want to go and look for that ghost. VO 33 Mother Nature has reclaimed this land. The hospital now a monument to decay and neglect. It’s hard to imagine its doors ever reopening. LINK: What I can see here is that this place is not unoccupied. People are coming through here. This is cables that have been stripped. You see. That has nothing to do with ghosts. That’s criminality. VO 34 For Dr Nick Wolmarans, Kempton Park Hospital isn’t just an abandoned building. It’s a painful symbol of squandered resources and a system failing the people it was meant to serve. UPSOUND Dr Nick Wolmarans: It’s a shame that a hospital and a facility went down the drain. I'm very concerned. I’ve been to a few of the government hospitals and I must tell you. (Subtitles) You must take your Bible and pray.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Dubbed South Africa's ghost hospital, the Kempton Park hospital closed in 1996. Since then it's become a destination for thrill seekers, but its draining millions from the public purse.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Kempton Park Hospital, a vast, decaying landmark closed suddenly in 1996 and was left to rot for nearly three decades. Once a state-of-the-art facility, it is now dubbed South Africa’s “ghost hospital,” known as much for its haunted reputation and thrill-seeking trespassers as for the millions it still drains from the public purse.
metadata.Summary: The hospital has become the stuff of legend. Ghostly sightings and a disgraced doctor have become folklore and paranormal “hunters” allegedly bribe guards to gain access. On the social media platform TikTok, dozens of videos showing the inside of the hospital have been posted. Comments on the posts indicate security guards were bribed between R50 and R150 to gain access. The Gauteng Department of Health spends over five million rand a year on security (revealed in a provincial legislature reply), yet the site has been stripped bare. Patients at Tembisa Hospital just 22 minutes away sleep on chairs and floors. Those living in Kempton Park are referred to Tembisa hospital, where conditions are dire. Yet, the Heatlh Department’s promises to refurbish the Kempton Park hospital have come to nothing. Ideas of refurbishing, demolishing or rebuilding, have gone nowhere. Costs ranged from 1,7 billion to 3,6 billion. Costs for security have ballooned to R35 million since its closure in 1996. The Democratic Alliance's Michael Waters, who inspected the site recently, said the building is an empty shell, with broken windows, ripped-out electrical outlets, smashed furniture and graffiti on the walls. He said it's clear the building has been illegally invaded, and something needs to be done urgently. Mother nature has taken over the site, and its clear that money is not being spent on the grounds. This is visible outside the hospital, where the land has become completely overgrown. Ghost tour operators have been doing tours of the hospital - a content creation company called Space did a series of videos of haunted places in Joburg, and visited Kempton Park hospital with a ghost tour operator. The videos show clear evidence of ash from recently burnt fires. It's seems access, if you are willing to bribe the security guards, is not an issue. On Halloween, it apparently gets very busy as hunters of the paranormal seek their thrills at the abandoned hospital.
metadata.Further information: We speak to the DA's Michael Waters about the millions being drained from the public purse, we also speak to ghost tour operator Nigel Mullinder and surgeon Dr Nick Wolmarans who worked at the hospital for a decade. Local GPs complain that they must refer Kempton Park patients to Tembisa hospital, when once they could simply send them to the Kempton Park hospital, a state of the art facility. We also gain access to the hospital ourselves and interview officials at the Gauteng department of Health about their plans for its future. Despite being given the run around, we are finally given access to the premises on the 13th of November with a delegation from the health department to escort us. The department denies bribery is happening, and say since they took over the security at the hospital in September 2024, with a company called Special Arrow Trade and Projects, the vandalism has stopped. In a response to a question in the provincial legislature, the Gauteng Health Department said it is still weighing options for the long-abandoned Kempton Park Hospital, with costs estimated at R1.76 billion to refurbish or R3.6 billion to demolish and rebuild. An Expression of Interest has been advertised to test private sector partnerships and alternative funding. Meanwhile, the facility continues to drain public funds, with R5.3 million spent on security in 2024/25 alone, bringing the total since May 2024 to R5.8 million. Nearby hospitals strain under pressure — Tembisa has 840 beds and Edenvale just 230 - underscoring the urgent need for decisive action on the so-called “ghost hospital.”
